newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says oil earnings $2.67 billion above budget.
newsitem.headline: Iran says oil earnings $2.67 billion above budget.

text.p: Iran has earned $2.67 billion in surplus oil revenue in the first nine months of the current Iranian year which started in March, an official at the National Iranian Oil Co. (NIOC) said on Monday.

Hojjatollah Ghanimifard, NIOC's director of international affairs, said this was 22.3 percent higher than planned crude oil and refined product revenue in the budget that was based on an average price of $15.50 a barrel.
Iranian crude prices have topped $20 a barrel in recent months as firmer international petroleum prices touched their highest level since the 1990-91 crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
OPEC-member Iran is the world's third largest crude exporter, exporting about 2.5 million barrels per day of crude to the international market.
Oil exports, Tehran's main foreign currency earner, were originally expected to bring in just under $16 billion in the current Iranian year ending on March 20.

The proposed budget for the next Iranian year is based on an average price of $17.50 a barrel for Iran's four main crude export grades -- Iran Heavy, Iran Light, Foroozan Blend and Lavan Blend -- Ghanimifard said.
